text:
sam: Heads up — noticed a spike in schema-rejects for fncall tool `payment_processor` around 15:03 UTC. A bunch of dedicated tenants hit quota fallbacks and we started returning non-JSON tool responses (schema mismatch + fallback). Looks correlated with autoscale events.
priya: Oof. Any sample payloads or validation errors?
sam: Pasting one short example:```json
request: {"tool":"payment_processor","input":"charge 12.50 usd"}
response: {"status":"ERR","detail":"timeout fallback: plain-text confirmation sent"}
validation_error: {"code":"TOOL_OUTPUT_NOT_OBJECT","msg":"expected object with fields [status, txn_id], got string"}
```
kevin: Was that because we ran out of tool adapters or because strict schema enforcement kicked in while fallback fired? There are two different action paths.
matt: Also want to understand customer-visible UX — some tenants saw a 4xx-ish error/ rejection in app, others got a degraded response. Which metric do we surface on console?
sam: Looking at logs: most of these are `validation_mode=strict` + `fallback_invoked=true` + `quota_state=burst_exhausted`. So I think strict validation is rejecting the fallback payload.
priya: Idea: add a "soft-validate" heuristic for rollouts/low-capacity situations — allow fallback string payloads to be proxied but mark them with a structured envelope so downstream can see validation failed. That preserves availability while surfacing the problem. Eg:```json
proxied_response: {"_redwood_fallback":true, "fallback_reason":"quota_exhausted","raw":"Payment processed: CONF12345"}
```
kevin: I like that. But we must ensure telemetry records: validation.strict=true/false, fallback.reason, and a counter for proxied_fallbacks. Otherwise ops won't know it's happening.
priya: Agreed. Proposed telemetry tags: `fncall_schema_valid=true|false`, `fallback_type=quota|timeout|adapter_error`, `proxied=true|false`. And increment `fncall_proxied_fallback_total{fallback_type=...}`
matt: For console UX, add a per-route gauge: "proxied fallback rate" and a small warning badge if >0.5% in last 1h. Also show last sample payload and which tenants experienced it.
kevin: How about rollout? We should gate soft-validate behind a feature-flag + canary. Steps: 1) enable telemetry and counters (no behavior change), 2) canary proxied=true for 1% traffic on non-critical tenants, 3) escalate to 10% if no regressions, 4) wide roll.
priya: We also need to record `validation_error_code` (TOOL_OUTPUT_NOT_OBJECT etc) as a label so we can query by root cause. Suggest sample query for Grafana: `sum by (validation_error_code) (increase(fncall_schema_reject_total[1h]))`
sam: Infra-bot, can you attach runbook for fallback handling?
infra-bot: Incident runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/fncall-fallbacks — sections: detection, mitigation (force-through proxied envelope), rollback flag, contact list. Auto-alert rule: trigger if `fncall_schema_reject_total` > 50 in 15m for dedicated cluster.
matt: Two op considerations: storage/retention of raw proxied payloads (PII risk). We need to strip sensitive fields or only keep hashes.
kevin: Agree. Envelope should include `raw_hash` and admin-only link to full payload (requires audit + consent). For immediate telemetry we can store `raw_hash` and truncated text.
priya: Action items: Sam -> implement proxied envelope + labels + counter (ETA 2d). Kevin -> add Grafana panels and alert rule (ETA 3d). Matt -> UX dials in console (warning badge + sample viewer; ETA 5d). Priya -> prepare rollout canary plan + compliance sign-off (ETA 2d).
sam: I'll open a PR with a small shim in the adapter layer that swaps strict-reject -> proxied envelope when `feature.soft_validate=true` and `quota_state!=ok`. Will include unit tests + example payload.
kevin: One more thing: let's tag all proxied events with `rollout_stage=canary|prod` so we can retire canary quickly.
matt: Sounds good. If nobody objects, I'll schedule the console change for next sprint. :thumbsup:
priya: No objections. Thanks all.
sam: Thanks — I'll post PR link when ready and drop a short note in #dedicated-notices for tenants that might see changed behavior.
